seo_title: Thomson Medical Case Study: Content for Parents | SOMIN
description: SOMIN read Thomson Medical and 6 competitors on content for Singapore parents and families, then built 6 pillars, 44 propositions and a 79-post calendar.
h1: Thomson Medical can own family moments the category still isn't publishing
lede: SOMIN read 12 monthly windows of organic content made for Singapore parents and families, August 2025 to July 2026, across Thomson Medical and 6 competitors including Mount Elizabeth, Gleneagles and KKH. It verified each trend against the prior year, mapped whitespace by cohort share, and built 6 pillars, 44 propositions, a 79-post calendar and 216 creative expressions.
meta_line: A SOMIN brand briefing · Aug 2025 to Jul 2026 · Singapore · Singapore Parents & Families

challenge.title: Where Thomson Medical can stand out against 6 Singapore hospitals
challenge.body: Thomson Medical competes with 6 Singapore hospitals for the attention of parents, mostly mothers aged 25 to 45, from pregnancy to school age. Competitors set the baseline every serious brand must cover. The question was which themes the category is moving toward that no one owns yet, and where Thomson Medical has the real-world permission to lead.

approach.title: 12 monthly windows checked against 4 prior-year quarterly cuts
points: Mapped Thomson Medical's real Singapore portfolio, from obstetrics, fertility and paediatrics to its 24-Hour Urgent Care Centre, to confirm the right to make each claim.
Classified organic posts made for Singapore Parents & Families across 7 brands, in 12 monthly windows from August 2025 to July 2026.
Checked each trend's direction against 4 prior-year quarterly cuts, so a single late spike is never shown as a confident trend.
Compared brand and competitor share within each cohort to sort themes into whitespace, partial, emerging and brand-owned.
Built a persona, tension, angle, story and proposition chain for each of 6 pillars.

findings_title: Open, rising and already-owned themes in family health content

findings.title: Family togetherness is open ground
findings.body: Family Togetherness & Milestone-Making sits at 0% for Thomson Medical and 0% for competitors, yet the underlying content drew 1,865,612 engagements across 85 of 270 evidence posts.

findings.title: New-parenthood anxiety is a verified rise
findings.body: The theme went from 0 to 26.5 items per window, peaking at 35 in January 2026, and was absent from all 4 prior-year quarterly cuts.

findings.title: Health awareness is already owned
findings.body: Health Awareness & Early-Detection Gaps makes up 25.3% of Thomson Medical's content against 13.5% for competitors. As a brand-owned core theme, it was left off the pillar shortlist.

delivered.title: Thomson Medical's 6 pillars, 44 propositions and 79-post calendar
points: 6 editorial pillars, ranked by whitespace and trend strength, each with its own persona, tension, angle and story
44 propositions built on real reasons to believe, such as 45+ years of maternity and paediatric care since 1979
A 79-post publishing calendar at 3 posts a week, with 5 lead posts, starting 11 August 2026
216 creative expressions across awareness, consideration and conversion, with 12 flagged as top-performer potential

quote.text: True connection blooms not in perfection, but in shared imperfections.

outcome.title: Lead with family togetherness and parental mental load
outcome.body: Lead with Family Togetherness & Milestone-Making and Parental Mental Load & Modern-Family Pressure, both sustained high across all 12 months, then test the emerging pillars while they are cheap to claim. Each pillar rests on a real Thomson Medical asset, from its 45+ year family health legacy to its 24-Hour Urgent Care Centre.

faq.a: Mount Alvernia, Mount Elizabeth, Gleneagles, Raffles Medical Group, KKH and NUHS, read alongside Thomson Medical on content made for Singapore Parents & Families.

faq.q: How does SOMIN decide what counts as whitespace?
faq.a: Brand-low alone is not whitespace. A theme qualifies only when the category is moving toward it, Thomson Medical is absent in content, and the brand has the real-world permission to lead.

faq.q: Does the briefing cover paid media?
faq.a: No. The scope was organic only, with whitespace and trend analysis. Paid and content-type tagging were not run in this engagement.
